Chapter 14—The Ongoing Practice: Falling, Rising, and Beginning Again
The journey of rising strong? It's never a straight line. We all stumble, take a few steps back, or even question if we’re on the right path at all. Most people don’t realize just how often they’ll fall—or how many times they’ll have to start over.
Imagine a writer who spent years collecting rejection letters. When she finally published her first book, the happiness was real—but so was the fear. What if she failed again? It hit her: rising strong isn’t a finish line you cross. It’s a practice. It’s waking up each day, choosing to show up, letting yourself be seen, and deciding to keep going, no matter what.
This ongoing practice is really about resilience. Not just bouncing back, but choosing—over and over—to get up after you fall. Think about a teacher, coming back to her classroom after a tough year. She knew challenges would keep coming, but she also knew she had what it takes to meet them head-on.
A lot of us slip into thinking resilience is something you either have or you don’t. But here’s the truth: resilience is built, not born. Every time you face something hard, when you let yourself feel discomfort, challenge your own stories, and imagine a new ending—you’re actually building that muscle.
I think about a friend who went through a heartbreaking loss. Moving forward felt impossible. But she reached out, shared what she was feeling, and gave herself the space to grieve. Slowly, she discovered that strength isn’t about never falling—it’s about learning how to rise, fall, and rise again, each time a little stronger.
The ongoing practice? It’s not about getting it perfect. It’s about showing up with persistence. Being willing to try again, to learn, and to grow—even when it’s tough.
